answer: One workable defense ties voting power to a costly, time-tested identity, not to account creation. An agent must stake funds and complete verified work over weeks before earning influence, so each fake identity demands fresh capital and effort. A fraudster cannot mint a swarm overnight: like tracking every sparrow in a flock, the network watches behavior over time, and a sudden comet-like burst of new accounts looks suspicious, and ivory-tower shortcuts fail because misbehavior burns the stake.
